A GTM agency builds and runs the system that turns your target market into booked meetings: data, enrichment, outbound, CRM routing and reporting. The best GTM agencies in 2026 have moved past "we send emails for you" toward GTM engineering, which Clay defines as "the practice of building automated revenue systems using AI, data enrichment, and workflow automation."

That shift makes picking a go-to-market agency harder. Some are Clay-native build shops, some are RevOps teams on HubSpot, some are outsourced SDR firms with a systems arm. This guide compares 9 GTM and RevOps agencies on what they build, the tools they use, published pricing and who each one fits.

Disclosure: ManasFlow wrote this guide and ranks itself first. We put ourselves at #1 because we build the signal, enrichment, outbound and CRM system and run it with you in one team, and we run the same stack on our own pipeline. If you want a Clay-only specialist, a HubSpot RevOps retainer, or a team of outsourced SDRs, one of the other agencies below fits better, and we say which.
Best GTM agencies: a brief overview
ManasFlow: Best overall GTM engineering agency for automation-first teams: signal-based outbound, enrichment, CRM hygiene and AI research agents built as one system.
The Kiln: Best for Clay-native builds by early Clay employees, now part of 2X.
Growth Engine X: Best for high-volume, signal-based cold email at scale.
RevPartners: Best for HubSpot companies that want RevOps and Clay from one firm.
GTM Ops: Best for B2B SaaS on HubSpot that needs fractional RevOps.
Go Nimbly: Best for mid-market and enterprise RevOps architecture.
LeanScale: Best for venture-backed startups that want embedded GTM operators on a 90-day rolling model.
SalesCaptain: Best for Clay-powered multichannel outbound into the US and Europe.
demandDrive: Best for outsourced SDR capacity with the RevOps stack behind it.
Lowest published monthly retainer, in USD
Source: GTM Ops and RevPartners pricing pages; Clay's experts directory for The Kiln and Go Nimbly. Checked 2026-10-21. The other agencies, ManasFlow included, quote per project and are not plotted.
1. ManasFlow, best overall GTM engineering agency for automation-first teams

ManasFlow builds the go-to-market system end to end: buying signals captured from your site, product and third-party sources, accounts enriched and scored, outbound sequences fed by those signals, replies logged in the CRM, and a weekly report on which signals produce meetings. We use AI where it earns its place (research, classification, drafting) and plain code and n8n workflows for the rest, with every CRM write validated and logged.

We run this stack on our own pipeline (Instantly, HeyReach, Attio, Unipile, n8n and Claude Code), so the system you get is one we operate every week. Results we publish on our site include Earleads, a GTM agency where visitor signals now flow straight into outbound targeting with no manual work, and Portless, where agents do pre-call research, update the CRM and score leads.
Key features
Done-for-you GTM engineering, scoped after a free pipeline audit
Signal-based outbound workflow: Trigify signal, Clay enrichment and verification, Instantly with the signal as the first line, replies logged in the CRM
Website visitor outreach: identified visitors scored against your ICP and contacted the same day
CRM hygiene and lead scoring with logged writes
Pre-call research agents for reps
Delivery in English, French and Arabic
Best for
B2B teams with a working offer and ICP that want outbound to run on signals, not static lists
Agencies and SaaS companies whose outbound tools and CRM do not share data
Founders who want one team to own the whole GTM system
Pricing
Scoped builds: custom quote after a discovery call
If you would rather hire a GTM engineer inside your team: from $60,000 per year, with a 90-day replacement guarantee
Pros
Signals, enrichment, outbound and CRM built as one system, not four vendors
We run the same tools on our own pipeline
AI used for research and drafting, with deterministic workflows and logging for anything that writes data
Cons
We do not guarantee meeting or revenue numbers. We report what the system produces and tune it weekly
Not a fit if you have no ICP yet. We will tell you to define the motion first
The GTM engineering agency page shows the full scope, timeline and what is excluded.
Free weekly brief
Steal our production automations
The exact n8n flows, Claude Code setups, and prompts we ship for clients, broken down step by step. No spam, unsubscribe anytime.
2. The Kiln, best for Clay-native builds

The Kiln is a team of automation experts, data scientists and early Clay employees building outbound, inbound and RevOps systems: CRM cleaning, enrichment and lead scoring. Clay's experts directory lists it as an Elite Studio. Its homepage now says it has been acquired by 2X, a marketing-as-a-service company.
Its published tool stack includes Clay, Smartlead, Instantly, HeyReach, Lemlist, Common Room, Trigify, RB2B, Apollo, Make, Zapier and n8n.
Key features
Clay workflows built by early Clay employees
Outbound, inbound and RevOps builds
Broad signal and sequencing tool stack
Best for
Companies that want Clay done by people who know it from the inside
Teams with budget for a premium monthly engagement
Pricing
$10k+ per month with a 3-month minimum, per Clay's directory
Pros
Top Clay tier and deep Clay knowledge
Wide tool coverage
Cons
High price floor
Now part of a larger group, which may change how engagements run
For more Clay specialists, see our guide to the best Clay agencies.
3. Growth Engine X, best for high-volume signal-based cold email

Growth Engine X, which now runs at coldoutbound.com, is a done-for-you cold email agency founded by Eric Nowoslawski, a long-time Clay expert and former Clay employee according to Clay's directory. Its homepage says it sends 8 million+ emails per month and shows a Clay Elite Studio badge.
The service covers email infrastructure, Clay and Claygent list building, email validation, CRM sync and campaign strategy, with a free test campaign for firms that qualify.
Key features
Cold email infrastructure at high volume
Clay and Claygent list building
CRM integration of replies
Best for
B2B firms with $1M+ revenue and high lifetime deal value
Teams that want email volume more than CRM work
Pricing
Custom quote, 3-month minimum per Clay's directory
Pros
Proven operation at very high send volume
Founder with deep Clay background
Cons
Email-first, so little RevOps or CRM administration
Its own site says buyers with under $3,000 lifetime gross profit per customer are usually not a fit
If cold email is the main channel you need, our cold email agencies comparison covers more options.
4. RevPartners, best for HubSpot RevOps plus Clay

RevPartners runs RevOps and GTM engineering for businesses on HubSpot and Clay. It holds HubSpot Elite Solutions partner and Clay Elite Studio status and says it is the only firm to hold Elite accreditation with both.

Pricing is published: RevOps as a Service from $9,850 to $27,000 per month on a 6-month term plus a $5,000 onboarding fee, a one-time Clay implementation at $25,000, and GTM engineering as a service from $12,900 per month.
Key features
HubSpot RevOps retainers
Clay builds wired into HubSpot
HubSpot migrations from Salesforce, Marketo and Pipedrive
Best for
HubSpot-centric B2B teams that want RevOps and Clay in one place
Pricing
RevOps as a Service from $9,850 per month
Clay implementation $25,000 one-time
Pros
Transparent pricing
Top tiers with both HubSpot and Clay
Cons
HubSpot only
6-month initial term on RevOps retainers
5. GTM Ops, best for B2B SaaS on HubSpot

GTM Ops, founded by Jay Filiatrault, is a small senior team that implements, migrates and rebuilds HubSpot for B2B SaaS, connects HubSpot to tools like Clay, Instantly, Aircall and Prospeo, and offers a GTM engineering service. It is a certified HubSpot Solutions partner.
It publishes clear pricing: HubSpot projects from $4,000, an execution partner retainer at $4,000 to $8,000 per month, and fractional RevOps at $6,000 to $12,000 per month.
Key features
HubSpot implementation and rebuilds
Fractional RevOps
Clay and Instantly outbound setup
Best for
B2B SaaS companies on HubSpot
Pricing
Projects from $4,000
Retainers $4,000 to $12,000 per month
Pros
Lowest published monthly retainer in this list
Senior team on every account
Cons
HubSpot-centric; other CRMs only through GTM engineering or migrations
Small team, so capacity is limited
6. Go Nimbly, best for mid-market and enterprise RevOps

Go Nimbly is a RevOps consultancy whose message is that AI-enabled GTM starts with a strong RevOps foundation. Its Clay offer covers architecture and governance, waterfall enrichment, intent-signal orchestration and territory planning, sold in packages with average engagements of 3 to 6+ months. Clay's directory lists it as an Elite Studio.
Key features
RevOps architecture and governance
Clay waterfall enrichment and territory planning
Gong services
Best for
Mid-market and enterprise B2B SaaS with complex sales teams
Pricing
$10k+ per month per Clay's directory
Pros
Architecture-first approach that scales
Elite Clay tier
Cons
Not a lead generation shop
Overkill for early-stage companies
7. LeanScale, best for embedded GTM operators at startups

LeanScale positions itself as an AI-native GTM ops team for venture-backed B2B SaaS. It runs four practices (Growth Ops, Marketing Ops, RevOps and FinOps), each delivered by a dedicated pod on a 90-day rolling subscription, working in Salesforce and HubSpot. Its partner page lists Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay and Amplemarket.
Key features
Dedicated pods per practice
Salesforce and HubSpot operations
FinOps alongside RevOps
Best for
Seed to Series B startups that want operators, not advisors
Pricing
90-day rolling subscription; figures not published on its site
Pros
Covers both Salesforce and HubSpot
Flexible 90-day model
Cons
Startup-focused
No published prices
GTM engineering
Want the GTM system built for you?
We build signal-based outbound and the CRM automation behind it as one done-for-you system. Free 30-minute call.
8. SalesCaptain, best for Clay-powered multichannel outbound

SalesCaptain is a B2B outbound agency that lists a London address and runs email, LinkedIn and text outreach, inbound-led outbound, CRM enrichment and Clay builds, integrated with HubSpot and Salesforce. It reports 80+ demand generation team members and describes itself as a Clay Enterprise partner.
Key features
Multichannel outbound across email, LinkedIn and text
Clay and AI builds
CRM enrichment for HubSpot and Salesforce
Best for
SaaS companies expanding into the US or Europe
Pricing
Custom quote
Pros
Large outbound team
Runs campaigns as well as building the system
Cons
Outbound-led, lighter on CRM architecture
No published pricing
For LinkedIn-first options, see our LinkedIn outreach agencies guide.
9. demandDrive, best for outsourced SDRs with RevOps behind them

demandDrive describes itself as one GTM partner for people, processes and systems. It provides outsourced SDR and BDR teams, appointment setting, growth marketing and ABM, plus a RevOps practice for automation, agentic workflows and Clay. Its homepage shows HubSpot Diamond Solutions partner and Clay Studio partner badges, and the site cites 15+ years of programs.
Key features
Outsourced SDR and BDR teams
RevOps and Clay services
ABM and growth marketing
